summary: multyproccess typosquat executes bundled infostealer payload on pip install
details: multyproccess@2.32.3 is a typosquat of the stdlib name 'multiprocessing' that ships a malicious install-time payload. setup.py registers a custom install/develop cmdclass (PostInstallCommand) that, on `pip install`, spawns a background thread which reads request/.payload, base64-decodes it, and passes the result to exec() with errors swallowed. The decoded blob is a Python infostealer that targets Chromium and Firefox login/cookie/autofill/credit-card stores (including Chrome v20 ABE bypass), 50+ browser-extension and standalone crypto wallets, FTP and email credentials, clipboard contents, screenshots, and keystrokes, and establishes persistence as a fake svchost.exe. Collected data is exfiltrated to api.telegram.org bot endpoints (sendMessage, sendDocument) and to a remote endpoint at recloud-blush.vercel.app, with host fingerprinting via ipinfo.io. Package metadata forges author='Python Software Foundation' and url='https://github.com/psf/request', and request/__init__.py shims the 'requests' API as a facade over the payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
